claims.statement: For every finite ordinary tree T and natural p with x(T)+2<=p and 3p<2alpha(T)+1, the fixed-selector weighted bipartite graph from independent (p+1)-sets to independent p-sets, with supplies and capacities w_F and all deletion and exact two-for-one switch arcs, admits an integral flow saturating every upper supply.
claims.scope: Universal ordinary-tree claim under the exact lower-region guards and fixed original selector stated in the common contract.
claims.reason: Literal exact computations on five asymmetric trees of orders 16, 17, 18, 22, and 23 at p=x+2 all saturated the upper supply. This bounded sample found no deficient cut and supplies no universal proof; selector losses were not tested.

limitations: The five hand-selected trees do not form an exhaustive census or a generation-complete family.
All tested leaves were favorable, and the tested ranks were only p=x+2; selector-loss cases and other eligible ranks remain unexamined.
The saturated finite flows neither prove the universal weighted Hall mechanism nor decide the primary aggregate.
